findings.text: Planning Code §762 classifies Bar as a conditional use (C) on the first story in NCT-VALENCIA zoning district, requiring a Conditional Use Authorization from the Planning Commission.

The Mission Alcoholic Beverage Special Use District (§249.60) permits a new or relocated Bar only as a conditional use and only if the operator uses a liquor license transferred from another Bar within the SUD.
An active ABC Type 41 (on-sale beer and wine, eating place) license is on file at 995 Valencia St, issued November 3, 2023 to Sarita's Grill & Beer.

In 2011 Planning approved CUA 2011.0255C to change an existing full-service restaurant at 991-999 Valencia St from a Type 41 to a Type 47 license, demonstrating that this address has been approved for alcohol service but as a restaurant use.

findings.text: Only 3 dated use decisions for bar-type businesses were found within 1,000 ft in the last 10 years (N=3): 1 approved, 0 approved with conditions, 0 denied, 2 withdrawn, which is too few to establish an approval rate.

A CUA application for a bar within a full-service restaurant at 970-974 Valencia St (66 m away, NCT-VALENCIA) was withdrawn in January 2011, and a CUA for a restaurant with Type 41 and live entertainment at 2519 Mission St (210 m, NCT-MISSION) was withdrawn in October 2019.

findings.verification_note: Catalog says Type 42 is non-quota and ABC issues new ones directly, and that 'nearly every city treats a Type 42 as a bar use that needs a conditional use permit or police/planning review before ABC will issue.' The generalization 'nearly…

findings.verification_note: Record shows 51 active on-sale licenses within 1,000 ft and undue concentration flag. The note says 'expect ABC to require' but the sentence says 'will require'—a firmer prediction than the record states.

findings.text: Nine active on-sale licenses exist within 500 ft of this address, including one Type 41 at 995 Valencia (the current tenant), two Type 47 licenses, one Type 21 off-sale, and five additional Type 41 licenses at nearby restaurants.
ABC's timeline for a Type 42 is typically 60-120 days if unprotested, but local protests or undue-concentration findings add 1-3 months for the PCN process.

Whether the existing Type 41 license at 995 Valencia can be upgraded to a Type 42 or a new Type 42 must be applied for depends on the change-of-ownership and business-entity structure, which the records do not show.

Amados at 998 Valencia St (31 m away) holds an active Place of Entertainment permit and operates with a Type 47 license in NCT-VALENCIA within the Mission Alcohol SUD.

Nearby POE permits have been approved when entertainment is framed as accessory or secondary to a primary food-service or retail use, with conditions on hours, sound levels, and good-neighbor policies.

zoning.name: Valencia Street Neighborhood Commercial Transit District
zoning.rules: Bar requires Conditional Use Authorization; Restaurant principally permitted (First Story). Bar C on the First Story only; Liquor Store NP; within the Mission Alcoholic Beverage SUD (§ 249.60), a new Bar must use a license transferred from another Bar in the SUD.

overlays.name: Mission Alcoholic Beverage Special Use District
overlays.effect: No new Liquor Stores. A Restaurant operating as a Bona Fide Eating Place may serve alcohol (licenses may be transferred in from inside or outside the SUD), as may non-profit theaters, bowling alleys/mini-golf with an integrated Restaurant, single-screen movie theaters (beer and wine) and ABC Type 90 music venues. A new or relocated Bar is considered under the underlying zoning but only as a Conditional Use, and must use a liquor license transferred from another Bar within the SUD. Existing liquor establishments may relocate or expand only with CU. East of the western boundary of the Mission Street NCT and north of Cesar Chavez Street, any new Restaurant requires CU and new ABC Type 75 (brewpub) licenses are prohibited. Good-neighbor operating conditions (§ 202.2 plus lighting and window-signage limits) apply.

expected_conditions.condition: ABC license restricted to beer and wine service only (Type 42), with no spirits or full-bar service unless a Type 47 or Type 48 license is obtained and approved by Planning.
expected_conditions.basis: The concept profile specifies beer and wine only, and the catalog confirms that Type 42 covers on-sale beer and wine at public premises. Any upgrade to full liquor would require a quota license (Type 47 or 48) and a new or amended CUA.

expected_conditions.condition: Bona fide meal service during all hours alcohol is served, with a full menu available and food sales accounting for a substantial portion of gross receipts, if the use is classified as a restaurant rather than a bar.
expected_conditions.basis: If the operator seeks to avoid the bar-CUA requirement by framing the use as a restaurant with incidental alcohol service, ABC and Planning will require proof of bona fide eating place status under ABC rules and Planning Code §102, including waiter service, a full kitchen, and meal availability during all alcohol-service hours.

expected_conditions.condition: Security plan detailing staffing, ID checks, queue management, and procedures to prevent over-service and manage patron behavior, particularly after 10 pm.
expected_conditions.basis: Entertainment Commission POE permits and Planning CUAs for bar and late-night uses commonly require security plans. The high density of bars and the undue-concentration flag suggest both agencies will scrutinize public-safety measures.
expected_conditions.verification_note: Catalog mentions security in general terms but does not state that POE permits or CUAs 'commonly require security plans' as a condition. The density record and catalog do not state this expected condition.

expected_conditions.condition: No dancing allowed unless the POE permit explicitly authorizes it; if dancing is proposed later, an amended POE application and potentially an amended CUA will be required.
expected_conditions.basis: The concept profile states no dancing, and the catalog distinguishes POE permits (which cover live entertainment and amplified sound) from nightclub uses that include dancing. Any material change adding dancing would trigger new discretionary review.

filing_playbook.action: Form the legal entity (LLC or corporation) with the California Secretary of State and obtain a federal EIN from the IRS.
filing_playbook.what_to_say: File Articles of Organization (LLC-1, $70) or Articles of Incorporation (ARTS-GS, $100) online through bizfileOnline. Within 90 days file the Statement of Information ($20 for LLC, $25 for corporation). Apply for the EIN immediately online at irs.gov (free, issued same day Mon-Fri). The entity name and EIN are required for every subsequent registration, the bank account, the lease, and the ABC application.

filing_playbook.action: Register for a San Francisco Business Registration Certificate and file a fictitious business name (DBA) statement with the County Clerk.
filing_playbook.what_to_say: Register online with the SF Treasurer & Tax Collector within 30 days of starting business; the fee is $55-$700 depending on projected gross receipts (e.g., $95 for up to $250k) plus a $4 state fee. You will receive a Business Account Number (BAN) that every other city department requires. File the FBN statement in person or by mail with the County Clerk (with photo ID), then publish it once a week for four weeks in a court-approved newspaper and file proof of publication within 45 days. Banks and ABC want the filed DBA statement.

filing_playbook.action: Schedule a pre-application meeting with SF Planning Department staff to confirm whether this wine bar with limited kitchen is classified as a bar (requiring CUA) or as a restaurant with incidental alcohol service (principally permitted), and to understand the Mission Alcohol SUD license-transfer re…

Bring the concept summary (40-seat wine bar, limited kitchen, beer-wine only, live music until 1 am), the lease or letter of intent for 995 Valencia St, and ask: (1) Does this qualify as a bona fide eating place (restaurant) or a bar under Planning Code §102? (2) If classified as a bar, must the ABC license be transferred from another bar within the Mission Alcohol SUD per §249.60? (3) What CUA filing requirements, noticing, and timelines apply? (4) Can the existing Type 41 at this address be leveraged or must a new Type 42 be applied for?

filing_playbook.action: Complete the final inspections (DPH, DBI, Fire if assembly occupancy ≥50), obtain the Health Permit to Operate, and apply for ancillary licenses and registrations (RBS training, ASCAP/BMI, workers' comp, organics hauler, sign permit).

timeline_cost.path: Conditional Use Authorization (bar use) + Place of Entertainment permit + ABC Type 42 license with PCN finding + building permit and DPH plan check for limited-kitchen tenant improvements
timeline_cost.notes: The entitlement path for a 40-seat wine bar with limited kitchen and live music at 995 Valencia St requires: (1) Conditional Use Authorization for bar use in NCT-VALENCIA ($3,100-$15,000 depending on construction scope; 120-300 days including pre-application, noticing, environmental review, and hearing), (2) Place of Entertainment permit ($2,708; 45-120 days), (3) ABC Type 42 license ($1,000-$1,600; 60-150 days including a likely PCN finding that adds 1-3 months), (4) DPH plan check ($828-$2,207) and Health Permit ($470), (5) building permit for tenant improvements ($800-$15,000 depending on construction valuation; 14-120 days for plan review), and (6) ancillary state and federal registrations (entity, EIN, business registration, seller's permit, RBS, food handler cards, workers' comp, ASCAP/BMI: ~$500-$1,200 total). The CUA and POE permits are discretionary hearings whose outcomes cannot be predicted from the three comparable decisions in the base rate (N=3, too few for a rate). The critical path is the CUA (6-10 months) followed by the POE (2-4 months, filed after CUA approval) and ABC (3-6 months including PCN). Total timeline: 8-18 months from pre-application to opening if all approvals are granted on first hearing; 12-24+ months if the CUA or POE is continued, appealed, or denied and must be refiled. Government fees total approximately $9,350-$26,500 (CUA, POE, ABC, building permit, DPH, business registration, entity formation); add architect/design fees ($15,000-$40,000), construction costs (budget $100-$200/sq ft for kitchen and bar tenant improvements), and legal/consultant fees for CUA and POE representation ($10,000-$30,000). The Mission Alcohol SUD requirement that a new bar use a license transferred from another bar within the SUD may require purchasing an existing Type 42 or Type 48 license on the open market (prices vary widely; confirm availability with a license broker) rather than applying for a new Type 42, which would add $20,000-$100,000+ to the budget and 90-180 days for escrow and transfer. Confirm the bar-versus-restaurant classification and SUD transfer requirement with Planning before signing the lease or paying CUA and ABC application fees.

records_summary: 995 Valencia St sits in the NCT-VALENCIA district where bars require Conditional Use Authorization, and critically, lies within the Mission Alcoholic Beverage Special Use District which requires any new or relocated bar to use a liquor license transferred from another bar within the SUD. The site has operated as a full-service restaurant (Sarita's Grill & Beer) with an active ABC Type 41 since 2023 and previously held a Type 47 from 2011–2023. The immediate area is saturated: 24 food/drink businesses and 9 active on-sale ABC licenses within 500 ft, 51 licenses within 1,000 ft, triggering ABC's undue-concentration flag and likely requiring a Public Convenience or Necessity finding from the City. Only 3 comparable dated use decisions were found within 1,000 ft in the last 10 years—too few to establish an approval rate.
